title: Log Integrity Gap — Core Switch Inspection

fields.organization: North Coast Regional Airport Authority — IT Operations
fields.location: Main Server Room, Rack 4 (Core Switch: NCIA-PACS-CORE)
fields.summary: While performing a routine audit of the core switch's log retention for compliance verification, a 4-hour gap was identified in the system logs from 22 October 2026, 22:00–02:00. The logs abruptly cease at 22:00 and resume at 02:00 with no error, reboot, or system interruption recorded in the event log. No hardware failure, power fluctuation, or maintenance window was logged during that period.

findings.notes: Log data missing for 04:00 between 22:00 and 02:00 on 22 October 2026.

findings.item: Event log — system reboot or crash
findings.notes: No reboot, crash, or power loss event recorded in logs for the same period.
Log rotation set to daily; no configuration error found.
Version 12.4.3a, up to date.
Syslog server (10.66.0.10) reachable and receiving logs from other devices.
No abnormal traffic spikes detected on SecNet (VLAN 660) during gap window.
No unauthorized login attempts recorded in PACS server logs for the same timeframe.
No forced entry or unauthorized access to server room logged via ISC-Gate-N during the gap.
No admin session initiated from NCIA-ENROLL (10.66.0.50) during gap.
No log truncation or database corruption detected in SQL server logs.

actionsTaken: Documented log gap in system audit trail
Verified no reboot or hardware fault
Cross-checked with vendor logs — no reported issues
Notified IT Manager via internal channel (22:00–02:00 window not covered by alerting system)
recommendations: Conduct forensic log analysis on NCIA-PACS-CORE to identify root cause of gap
Audit all PACS system access logs for the 22 October 2026 window
Review vendor remote access logs for 22 October — prior to 22:00
Report to IT Leadership and Security Oversight Committee per ASP Section 3.4
fields.photosNote: 2 screenshots attached: (1) log output from NCIA-PACS-CORE (10.66.0.10), showing 4-hour void between 22:00 and 02:00; (2) timestamped console session from 13:28, showing no prior alert for the gap.

instructorNote: This inject introduces a forensic clue that suggests tampering or data suppression. The IT team should recognize that a 4-hour log gap with no system event is highly unusual and warrants immediate investigation. Watch for teams that dismiss it as 'just a buffer overflow' — the IT Manager will later claim this.
